project: Diagnose and Fix Silent Pre-Runtime Blocking After a Hard Kill
description: Reproduce the silent pre-runtime block that can follow a hard-killed you process, identify the actual retained serialization resource, and make same-scope successor startup either reclaim a provably orphaned resource or fail promptly with a non-success, actionable diagnostic naming the resource and safe clearing steps.

context.customerAsk: Diagnose and fix probe-finding backlog item 3 from docs/temp/progress.md: after a predecessor you process is hard-killed, a fresh session can block silently before runtime start. Reproduce it, add a functional regression test, and either recover automatically or fail fast with an actionable error naming the stale resource and how to clear it, while following docs/temp/scale-program-rules.md.
context.problem: A hard kill bypasses normal lifecycle cleanup, and a later process using the same local backend scope can encounter retained ownership or serialization state before runtime startup and wait without a bounded outcome or useful diagnostic. The suspected backend-scope serialization path has not yet been proven to be the actual source.
context.solution: Use deterministic real-process hard-kill evidence to identify the exact retained resource and owner, then make acquisition explicit and bounded at that owner: atomically reclaim only ownership proven orphaned, otherwise preserve the resource and return a typed non-success startup failure that identifies it and gives safe clearing instructions. Preserve active-owner exclusion and prove both hard-kill recovery/failure and live contention with focused and functional tests.

acceptanceCriteria: A deterministic functional scenario hard-kills a real predecessor after the relevant pre-runtime resource is acquired, then starts a successor against the same backend scope and proves the successor never waits indefinitely.
The implementation identifies and handles the actual retained resource found by reproduction; it does not encode backend-scope serialization as the cause unless evidence confirms it.

When ownership is provably orphaned, startup atomically reclaims it and reaches the normal runtime-start observation; if safe reclamation cannot be proven, startup returns a bounded non-success outcome whose stderr names the resource and gives concrete safe clearing instructions.
A live predecessor retains exclusive ownership: a competing successor neither steals nor removes its resource and instead receives the documented bounded contention outcome.

Startup acquisition, recovery, contention, and failure emit structured, safe diagnostics with the backend-scope identifier, resource identifier or path, outcome, and owner/liveness classification, without leaking work payloads or credentials.

Typecheck and focused package/functional tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, conflicts and shared-file churn are reconciled against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Give a successor a bounded outcome after predecessor hard kill
userStories.description: As an operator restarting you after a crash or hard kill, I want the successor to recover safely or stop with an actionable diagnostic so that startup can never hang silently before runtime begins.
acceptanceCriteria: A functional regression test uses a real OS process because hard-kill cleanup behavior cannot be proven through root.BuildProcess alone: it observes deterministic acquisition of the actual pre-runtime resource, hard-kills the predecessor, and launches a successor with the same home/config and Factory target.

The test uses an explicit acquisition/startup observation rather than a sleep, runs offline with deterministic injected or recorded external effects, and has a bounded test guard that reports captured stdout/stderr and process state on failure.

Reproduction evidence identifies the concrete serialization resource and its owning service; the fix remains in that owner, keeps ownership state explicit, and isolates filesystem/process/liveness side effects behind existing injected edges or a narrowly owned platform capability.
If predecessor ownership is provably orphaned, the successor atomically reclaims the resource and reaches the existing runtime-start observation without requiring manual cleanup.

If orphan status or safe reclamation cannot be established, the successor exits within the startup acquisition bound with a non-success result; stderr identifies the blocking resource or path and explains the exact safe steps to verify the old owner is stopped and clear that resource before retrying.

The normal no-residue startup path remains behaviorally unchanged, and no public API or generated-contract change is introduced unless the diagnostic cannot be represented by the existing typed startup failure path.
Focused owner-level tests and the hard-kill functional regression test pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Completed 2026-08-10: the real built-process regression observes the first durable config.json backendScopeID checkpoint and then the exact pre-runtime packaged-factory `.<factory>.staging-owner` acquisition, suspends the predecessor before inspecting that resource, hard-kills it while the acquisition barrier is held, and starts a same-HOME/same-scope successor. The owning System Initialization packaged-factory installer detects a pre-existing stage at the global Factory root, classifies it as `outcome=indeterminate-contention` with `owner_liveness=indeterminate`, preserves it, and returns a typed bounded startup failure. The CLI writes the exact resource path plus verify-no-owner/remove-only-that-path/retry guidance to stderr; the successor never reaches runtime. Focused owner tests and the repeated real-process test prove the resource is preserved without the former observe-then-suspend race. Backend-scope identity remains identity persistence, not an ownership lock. Live-owner and acquisition-race coverage is recorded under story 002.

userStories.title: Preserve live ownership and actionable contention diagnostics
userStories.description: As an operator with a you process that is still running, I want a competing process to respect its ownership and explain the contention promptly so that stale recovery cannot create two runtimes for one scope or destroy a live resource.
acceptanceCriteria: With the predecessor demonstrably live and holding the same resource, a successor does not delete, replace, or take ownership of that resource and does not reach runtime start.

The competing successor reaches a bounded non-success outcome whose stderr names the contended resource, identifies available owner evidence such as PID without assuming PID reuse proves identity, and explains how to stop or verify the owner before retrying.

Owner-liveness checks treat missing, malformed, reused, permission-denied, and racing ownership metadata conservatively; only a provably orphaned resource is reclaimed, and compare-and-reclaim behavior cannot remove ownership newly acquired by another process.

Structured operation diagnostics distinguish acquired, reclaimed-orphan, active-contention, indeterminate-contention, and failed outcomes using safe identifiers, while runtime-start output is emitted only after ownership succeeds.
Focused concurrent-owner tests deterministically cover the live-owner, indeterminate-owner, and acquisition-race paths without sleeps, deadlock, or leaked child processes/resources.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Completed 2026-08-10: packaged Factory create/replace now atomically reserves a deterministic `.<factory>.staging-owner` directory through a dedicated injected directory-creator edge and publishes PID metadata through the injected filesystem edge. The persisted backendScopeID is threaded from System Initialization into installation diagnostics. Valid existing targets retain the normal skip path without acquiring the write lease. Live owners produce bounded `outcome=active-contention` diagnostics with `owner_pid` and `owner_identity=unverified`; missing, malformed, permission-denied, and racing metadata remain preserved as indeterminate contention. An explicitly revalidated orphan is atomically claimed by renaming the exact old lease to a distinct staging-prefixed recovery path, publishing the successor owner there, and handing that lease to the installation; the deterministic concurrent orphan-reclaimer test proves a delayed contender gets `owner_liveness=racing` and cannot remove the winner's recovery resource. Structured logs distinguish acquired, success, reclaimed-orphan, active-contention, indeterminate-contention, and failed outcomes without work payloads or credentials. Focused tests deterministically cover structured scope logging, orphan revalidation, live owner, malformed/indeterminate metadata, acquisition race, and concurrent orphan reclaim; the real hard-kill process regression verifies the successor reports the retained owner resource and PID without reaching runtime. Review follow-up removed `--with-mock-workers` from the OS-boundary test, documented the two necessary filesystem observations, and restored unrelated full-flow generated churn.
